newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt lower on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt lower on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices extended losses across the board in late trade amid concerns that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan signaled an upcoming interest rate hike, market experts said.

"I think that (Greenspan's comments) is indeed the major factor that moved the market today in New York. It opened extremely firm but upon his comments there was a correction," said Kurt Schmid, executive director at SBC Warburg.
The biggest losers on the day were fixed-rate bonds rather than floating rate instruments, market sources noted.

At 1630 EST/2130 GMT, Argentine pars were 1-3/4 weaker at 67-1/2 bid and Mexican pars were 1-3/8 lower at 77-1/8 bid, whereas Argentine FRBs were 3/4 weaker at 91-1/2 bid and Mexican discount bonds were 1/8 softer at 92-5/8 bid.
"There was some demand for floaters and they should outperform fixed-rate instruments on an ascending interest rate environment," said a head trader a major U.S. investment bank in New York.
"Earlier in the day, we were outperforming Treasuries in terms of spreads. Now we are performing with Treasuries so the market is holding extremely well," said the head trader mentioned above.
At 1642 EST/2142 GMT, the U.S. Treasury long bond was down 1-17/32 at 98.02/03 yielding 6.78 percent.
Among other Brady bonds, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1-1/8 weaker at 81-1/8 bid and Venezuelan FLIRBS VZ6C97 were 1/2 lower at 92 bid.
Speaking before the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, Greenspan hinted that the central bank may have to raise interest rates in order to contain inflationary pressures.
Although some Brady instruments were hammered following Greenspan's comments, market experts said they believed prices would rebound following a few days of solid profit-taking.
"After some profit taking that will continue to unwind in the next couple of days I think the outlook is still favorable," said Paolo Leme, head of emerging markets research at Goldman Sachs & Co.

"The bottom line is that the market has done extremely well. It has continued to rally very vigorously over the last five days excluding today and any excuse for those that were on the sidelines or had position to take profits they found it today. I don't consider it to be a bearish testimony," Leme of Goldman added.
Market experts also noted that the emerging debt market, which has outperformed U.S. Treasuries for some time now, moved in tandem with Treasuries today and did not underperform the U.S. bond market.
Elsewhere, Russian Vneshconombank dollar denominated loans were 1-1/2 weaker at 84-7/8 bid and Bulgarian IABs were 1/2 softer at 61-7/8 bid.
